lines.text: Welcome, arcade engineer! Today you’ll learn how games make dozens of enemies, coins and raindrops from just one sprite.
A clone is a copy of a sprite, made while the program runs.
One Star sprite can make ten falling stars without you drawing ten sprites.
Every new clone runs the script under “when I start as a clone”.
Each clone can go to its own random place and move by itself.
Usually the original sprite hides and just makes clones — like a factory.
Each clone shows itself when it starts.
Delete clones when they are finished (for example, when they fall off the bottom).
Too many clones slow a game down — Scratch allows 300.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
